Subject: MAP kickoff - unit cost inputs we need

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the call this morning — good alignment overall. Procurement asked that we lock down the cost assumptions for the MAP before we circulate the final timeline to our finance team. Two things are blocking for them:

1) The tokens-per-dollar baseline you intend to use for the POC (we want a per-inference unit cost, not just a per-token average).
2) Any caching/prefetch/batching assumptions that materially change the cost profile (e.g., KV warmup, prefix caching, and how continuous batching affects latency SLOs).

Can you share a short preflight doc with the version of the model, quantization profile, and a simple sensitivity table (tokens/$ at 50/75/100 qps and 5/20/50% cache hit)? Also, procurement wants the canonical attachment list for the MAP so they can attach it to the SOW.

Appreciate it — looking to get this to budget by Friday so our legal/finance can start redlining.

Best,
Amelia
Director, Platform Integrations
Novafit

Subject: RE: MAP kickoff - unit cost inputs we need

Amelia — thanks, and totally understood. I attached a draft MAP workbook (novafit_map_draft.xlsx) with three tabs: baseline assumptions, sensitivity matrix, and a short narrative describing operational levers. High level:

- Model: open-mistral-7B-std (int8-llm quant profile we recommend for latency-sensitive interactive flows).
- Baseline tokens/$: 8.2k tokens per USD at 95% cache miss and average seq length 180. This is generated from our POC profile (shots with 128-token prompts + 180-token completions).
- With a 30% prefix cache hit the effective tokens/$ increases to ~11.7k (roughly linear for small hit rates in our sim).
- Batching: continuous batching reduces per-token overhead by ~18% at 60 qps compared to per-request execution in our sim; but it adds 15–25ms median queuing depending on traffic shape.

Key open questions for procurement/finance that we flagged in the workbook:
- Which latency SLO is non-negotiable (p50/p95)? If they require <120ms p95, we need to constrain batching aggressiveness.
- Do they want unit pricing to reflect worst-case cold starts (no cache) or amortized expected loads (with steady-state cache)?

I’m looping David and Markus for a brief technical appendix that explains how we ran the prefetch/prefill sims and where KV warmup shows up in the cost table.

Next steps: I’ll post the workbook to Drive and can publish a short 1-pager for procurement summarizing the three pricing profiles (conservative, expected, aggressive). Is Friday budget lock still the target?

Thanks — Rachel
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding a few tech notes for the appendix (copied into the workbook as a short methods section). Feel free to paste this into the MAP doc: 

- Prefetch / KV warmup: our simulator models a warmup window where recent prefixes are already populated in the KV cache. Warmup reduces compute per request for repeated workflows (chat histories, form-filling). For Novafit’s predicted 40% repeat-prefix traffic, we observed a ~22% reduction in aggregate GPU cycles.

- Cache hit modeling: we simulated cache hits at 0/10/30/50% and computed effective tokens/$ by dividing tokens generated by total GPU-seconds and applying our current price curve (hosted tiers). The relationship is roughly proportional for small hit deltas but sublinear as hits approach 80% due to tail effects (I included a short chart in prefetch_sim_results.csv).

- Batching: continuous batching lowers kernel overheads; however, the effective latency experienced by end-users depends on real-time arrival patterns. For bursty traffic (coeﬃcient of variation >1.5) batching yields ~20% cost improvement with p95 latency increase of ~40ms. For steady traffic batching delivers ~25% cost benefit with <15ms p95 increase.

- Quantization caveat: int8-llm here preserves quality for Novafit’s verification prompts but increases GPU memory pressure slightly; in corner cases (long context lengths >1.5k tokens) you'll see higher cost per token due to memory management.

Attachments: I attached the raw sim export and a brief README for the PoC.

-David
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Amelia — quick commercial note to pair with Rachel/David’s technical rundown:

- Pricing profiles (from workbook): Conservative (assume 0% cache hit; conservative batching) -> $0.0125 per 1k tokens (approx 8.0k tokens/$). Expected (30% cache hit + moderate batching) -> $0.009 per 1k tokens (approx 11.1k tokens/$). Aggressive (50%+ cache hit + full batching/quant) -> $0.0065 per 1k tokens (approx 15.4k tokens/$).

- For the MAP SOW we recommend listing the "Expected" profile as the baseline with an appendix that defines how actual usage will be reconciled (monthly reconciliation using sampling and a 30-day lookback cache hit measurement). That satisfies finance wanting a single number but keeps us transparent about the variance drivers.

- If Novafit wants tighter per-inference pricing (fixed unit price), we can propose a Reserved Capacity add-on (Dedicated) with a 12-month commit; I included a high-level comparator in the Drive sheet.

Request: can procurement confirm whether they prefer (A) a single amortized token rate in the SOW or (B) a two-line item with baseline tokens/$ + an adjustment clause tied to measured cache hit and average seq length? Option B is our preference for accuracy but procurement sometimes asks for A for simplicity.

If we get confirmation by EOD Friday we’ll finalize the MAP workbook, upload the SOW-ready attachments and send to your finance/legal teams.

Thanks — Ben
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
